cover.intro: A hypothetical completed review of an insurer's vehicle valuation, with a customer reconsideration request and an example of guidance after the insurer replies.
cover.conclusion_title: The evidence supports asking for reconsideration.
cover.conclusion: In this example, the insurer's $20,500 vehicle valuation sits below all five selected asking prices. The report also leaves a repeated condition deduction unexplained. Together, these points support a focused request for review.
cover.gap_note: $22,900 median asking price minus $20,500 insurer vehicle value. This is a comparison to discuss, not a promised increase or an amount determined to be owed.
cover.sample_note: All case details, people, insurer records, listings and prices are invented for this sample. No real customer records or live market searches were used. This packet brings the report and related customer guidance together; it is not an exact export of the application.

scope.intro: The review focuses on the vehicle value in the insurer's report and the evidence supporting it. It keeps that value separate from the customer's final settlement payment.
vehicle_facts: Customer reports normal pre-loss condition, no existing damage and standard XLE equipment. No physical inspection.
Subject V0; individual VINs omitted from this illustrative packet. All comparable records represent separate hypothetical vehicles.
records: September 8 report: $20,500 vehicle value; three comparables, disclosed adjustments and equal weighting. Reproduced on page 3.
Vehicle details and pre-loss condition statement shown above. Customer-reported facts are not independently inspected.
Five fictional historical asking-price observations for the loss date. The entire sample comparison set is on page 4.
September 23 hypothetical response, shown on page 7. It is separate from the September 18 original review.
scope.scope_note: The sample source IDs identify records described within this document, not externally retrieved documents. No actual insurer PDF, listing archive or VIN verification accompanies this example.
scope.boundary: Taxes, title or registration fees, deductible, loan payoff and other settlement items have not been evaluated or added. No net settlement check is calculated. No state-specific entitlement or deadline is determined.

insurer_review.intro: The hypothetical report uses three 2020 RAV4 XLE AWD vehicles. Its disclosed adjustments produce an equally weighted vehicle value of $20,500. The arithmetic works; the basis for some adjustments needs explanation.
insurer_review.table_note: All amounts are hypothetical USD. Adjustments above are the insurer's figures, not dollar adjustments calculated or endorsed by Venfour. Other disclosed adjustments are $0 in this example.
findings: The same $1,100 condition deduction appears three times.

R1 gives no itemized explanation for the deduction. C1 reports normal pre-loss condition. Ask what the deduction represents and what evidence supports it. Its repetition alone does not prove it is improper.
Mileage differences matter, but the adjustment method is unclear.

The insurer subtracts $400 for I1, adds $500 for I2 and subtracts $100 for I3. Those directions are consistent with their lower or higher mileage. The sample report does not explain the rates or method.
The insurer's result is below the separate market set.

All five selected historical asking prices are above $20,500. Ask the insurer to address the comparable records and explain any material differences. Asking prices alone do not establish completed-sale value.
insurer_review.priority: Priority: request the condition-adjustment basis and a written response to the five market records. Do not add the $1,100 deduction to the $2,400 asking-price gap; these are overlapping ways to examine the same valuation.

market_review.intro: Five separate hypothetical vehicles match the subject's year, model, trim and drivetrain. Each record is stipulated, for this example only, to have been advertised on the September 2 loss date.
market_review.table_note: Every row: 2020 Toyota RAV4 XLE AWD. Distances are illustrative miles from ZIP 60618. IDs H1-H5 replace identifying dealer and listing details; there are no live listing links in this sample.
market_review.selection: Venfour ranks vehicles by similarity, not price. This sample shows the complete comparison set: five separate hypothetical vehicles, with no duplicates, subject-vehicle matches or supplemental listings chosen for higher prices.
market_review.timing: Historical activity here is assumed for illustration, not verified. Venfour distinguishes loss-date records from current listings. A current listing does not establish that a vehicle was available at that price on the loss date.
market_review.limits: Asking prices are not verified sale prices. No independent dollar adjustments are made for mileage, condition, equipment, location, certification or warranty. Condition and optional equipment may differ. These vehicles do not represent the entire market.
market_review.record_note: A real case's available source details, dates and limitations matter. Missing evidence must remain missing; a sample ID or a current listing cannot substitute for historical verification.

reasoning.intro: The supported conclusion is a reason to question the insurer's current vehicle valuation. The evidence does not establish a new appraised value or a guaranteed settlement target.
steps: The $20,500 baseline is the insurer's vehicle valuation before separate settlement items. It is not a check after a deductible or loan payoff.
Compare it with the recorded market evidence.
The five hypothetical asking prices run from $22,400 to $23,400, with a $22,900 median. The insurer's value is $1,900 below the lowest asking price and $2,400 below the median.
Treat the gap as a review question.

The $2,400 median difference is about 11.7% of the insurer's $20,500 value. It shows the size of the discrepancy worth discussing. It does not isolate an insurer error or measure the amount the customer will recover.

A clearer explanation of the $1,100 condition deduction may resolve some of the difference. Removing that deduction would not, by itself, establish the market value. Do not count it again on top of the asking-price gap.
strategy: Attach the review and comparable evidence. Ask the adjuster to reconsider the vehicle value and explain the condition and mileage adjustments.
Ask for a written, itemized reply
Request an updated valuation report, or a brief explanation of why the current value is maintained and how the listed vehicles were considered.
Save the reply for the next review
Keep the sent request and attachments. When the insurer responds, add its exact reply, revised report and vehicle-value amount to the Venfour case.
reasoning.closing: A useful outcome may be a corrected value, a documented explanation or confirmation that more evidence is needed. The customer decides how to proceed.

request.intro: An example of the customer-controlled reconsideration request. The wording is complete for this hypothetical case; real claim details and attachments must be reviewed before sending.
request.subject: Request to review vehicle valuation - claim SAMPLE-TL-2026-01
paragraphs: Thank you for your help with my total-loss claim for my 2020 Toyota RAV4 XLE AWD. I reviewed the September 8 valuation report and would appreciate another look at the $20,500 vehicle valuation.

The attached review includes five comparable vehicles with asking prices from $22,400 to $23,400 and a median of $22,900. The records relate to the September 2 loss date. I understand these are asking prices rather than verified sale prices, and differences between vehicles may affect the comparison.

Could you please explain the $1,100 condition deduction applied to each of the three comparables and the evidence supporting it? I reported normal pre-loss condition and no existing damage. I would also appreciate an explanation of the mileage adjustments.

Please reconsider the vehicle valuation in light of the comparable records. If the valuation remains unchanged, could you explain how those vehicles were considered and which differences or adjustments support your conclusion? An updated valuation report or a written explanation would be helpful.
Thank you for your time and help,
request.attachments: For an actual claim: the customer's Venfour valuation report and its supporting comparable evidence. This sample packet and its invented records must not be submitted as evidence for a real claim.
request.send_note: The customer checks the recipient, claim number, facts and attachments, then sends the message through their own email or insurer channel. Venfour prepares guidance; it does not send to or negotiate directly with the insurer.

response.intro: This hypothetical continuation shows how a later insurer reply can be reviewed against the original request and saved evidence. It does not replace or rewrite the original report.
response.reply: We reviewed your request and revised the vehicle valuation to $21,300. We reduced the condition deduction from $1,100 to $300 for each comparable; the mileage adjustments and equal weighting remain unchanged. The vehicles you supplied are dealer asking prices, so we have retained our valuation method.
analysis: R2 states a revised vehicle value of $21,300 and a lower condition deduction. Check the amount and changes against the revised valuation report.

The insurer reconsidered the condition adjustment and correctly distinguishes dealer asking prices from sale prices. The reply should be acknowledged rather than treated as a rejection of every point.

R2 does not explain the remaining $300 deduction, the mileage method or how the individual market vehicles were evaluated. The revised value remains below the saved asking-price range; that fact alone does not decide whether to accept it.
response.recommendation: The saved conclusion assessed $20,500, not the new $21,300 amount. Venfour can explain the reply and unresolved points, but the original asking-price range does not establish whether this revised offer should be accepted or challenged further.
response.next: Confirm the revised report and amount, then decide whether to request clarification of the remaining adjustments. Where supported and available, Venfour can prepare a follow-up using the saved evidence. It does not calculate a new appraised value from the reply.

continuation.intro: The customer remains in control of the insurer conversation and the decision. Venfour organizes the evidence and helps interpret what the insurer says next.
steps: Mark the request as sent in the case and keep a copy of what was sent. The case moves to waiting for the insurer. Venfour does not contact the adjuster on the customer's behalf.
Paste the response or upload the original reply, and record any revised vehicle-value offer. Review the interpretation and check uncertain amounts against the original.
Choose whether to continue, review the prepared follow-up and send it yourself. Save subsequent replies in the case so the next review has the prior request and evidence.

The customer chooses the next step and confirms any acceptance with the insurer. Recording a decision in Venfour does not communicate acceptance to the insurer. The case retains its saved report, replies and history.
continuation.fee_intro: The package includes the review, downloadable report, supported reconsideration request and guidance after the insurer replies. No subscription. A higher valuation or settlement is not guaranteed.
refunds: If the completed review does not reasonably support a valuation dispute, the full fee is refunded automatically. The completed review and report remain available.

After following the Venfour-supported reconsideration process, the customer may request a full refund with sufficient final-outcome documentation within 30 days of the insurer's final written response. The threshold compares vehicle value at purchase with the final verified vehicle value, not the settlement check. An interim reply is not a final outcome.
continuation.attorney_note: For the referring attorney: this packet puts the vehicle-value baseline, adjustment questions, comparable evidence and customer correspondence in one readable record. It can reduce the work of organizing a client's property-damage valuation question while leaving legal advice and representation with counsel.
continuation.limits: Venfour is a self-service evidence review. It is not legal advice, an independent appraisal, a determination of what is owed or direct insurer negotiation. No claim outcome is promised.
